arguments.command:
cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

The change makes `full` the default: retain Unicode and quote CSV fields
containing commas, quotes, CR, or LF, without reordering columns. This is a
functional CLI regression study, not an instruction-following/model eval;
there is no historical policy instruction, provider, or token comparison.

## Observations

`test/results.json` contains actual stdout, exit status, source/fixture/runner
hashes, and runtime for the current artifact. Exact stdout (including its final
LF) is the grading contract. Valid alternative CSV quoting is deliberately not
accepted by this canonical-output test. Infrastructure errors are separate from
output mismatches. All current executions exited successfully.

| Case | Baseline | Full/default | Without Unicode | Without escaping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unicode | fail: data lost | pass | fail: data lost | pass |
| Escaping | fail: unescaped fields | pass | pass | fail: unescaped fields |
| Column order | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| Trailing whitespace | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| CR/LF | fail: unquoted breaks | pass | pass | fail: unquoted breaks |
| Empty row | pass | pass | pass | pass |

The initial revision (`082ca49`) default failed Unicode and escaping; its
explicit `full` mode already passed both. The prepared default-only revision
also already passed both. Both revisions failed the CR/LF case even with `full`;
this final revision additionally quotes CR. Thus Unicode/escaping improvements
are over the original default, not over its explicit full configuration or the
prepared revision. Historical executions were checked separately; transient
records remain in ignored local storage.

The original two development cases are reused diagnostics. Four added cases
are regression/synthetic edge coverage, not independent workload samples or
held-out statistical validation. Component ablations remove Unicode preservation
or quoting; all other logic and inputs remain identical. Baseline removes both.
No policy/empty-policy control applies to these executable configurations.
Ablation failures alone are not evidence of improvement over a prior revision.

## Reproduction

Requires Node.js (recorded run: v22.23.4), no packages or network:

```
node test/study.mjs --replay test/results.json
node test/study.mjs --run .local/new-results.json
```

Use a new output filename each run (existing records are never overwritten).
The runner freezes hashes before execution, interleaves conditions by case,
and checks source/inputs remain unchanged. Replay recalculates scores from
captured stdout without running the app; it does not assert the saved source
hash equals today's source. Fresh runs always execute today's `app.mjs`.
Grader self-tests run before execution, checking correct, incorrect,
noncanonical-but-equivalent CSV and whitespace-sensitive output. No manual
grading is needed. The suite assumes a JSON array of string-convertible values;
input validation and multirow exports are outside its scope.

The old local report's source hash was stale and its `trimEnd()` measurement
could hide whitespace loss. It is not used as current evidence. A first fresh
run exposed the CR regression; that failed capture is retained locally, not
silently replaced as if it had passed. The checked-in evidence contains only
public-safe task data and actual subprocess output. Private local runtime
metadata is omitted entirely; none is needed to reproduce these executions.
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export CLI

Run `node app.mjs '["Ada","Lin"]'`. Output is one CSV row in input order,
with Unicode preserved and commas, quotes, CR and LF escaped by default.
The optional final argument selects `baseline`, `full`, `without-unicode`, or
`without-escaping`. These are executable component configurations, not model
prompts. Baseline strips non-ASCII characters and does not escape fields.

Run the regression comparison with Node.js (no dependencies or network):

```
node test/study.mjs --replay test/results.json
node test/study.mjs --run .local/new-results.json
```

Fresh output paths must not already exist. See `REPORT.md` for grading scope,
per-case observations, baseline comparisons, and limitations. Local development
and audit records remain ignored in `.local/`.
EOF
